name: GitClaw (Gitagent)
vibe_summary: A git-native agent framework where identity, rules, memory, tools, and skills are all version-controlled files — fork an agent, branch a personality, git log its memory. Recently hardened with security fixes and a Rust rewrite ('ira') powering a Tauri desktop app.
best_for: Developers who want agent config, memory, and skills versioned in git
Teams forking/branching agent personalities like code
Users wanting a CLI + SDK + optional desktop app with local models via Ollama
avoid_if: You need a large, battle-tested community and plugin registry
You want zero-setup hosted agents with no API key management
You need proven sandboxing for untrusted multi-tenant workloads
openclaw_advantages: Git-native agent definition: identity, rules, and memory are diffable, forkable files
Recent security hardening (RCE fix, race fixes, leak-free cleanup) with regression tests
Rust port with Tauri desktop app and Ollama local-model management
MCP client support and slim supply-chain-friendly core package
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community (712 stars vs OpenClaw's massive ecosystem)
No multi-channel messaging (WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack) breadth like OpenClaw
No Reddit presence and thin third-party sentiment data
Mixed TS/Rust codebase history suggests architectural churn
confidence_summary: Evidence is moderate: README and commit history are detailed and show active, security-conscious development, but there is zero Reddit discussion and limited independent web coverage, so community sentiment and adoption claims are uncertain.

overview_markdown:
GitClaw (branded Gitagent) is a git-native AI agent framework: the agent itself is a git repository, with `agent.yaml` for config, `SOUL.md` for personality, `RULES.md` for constraints, and version-controlled `memory/`, `tools/`, `skills/`, and `hooks/` directories. This 'agents as repos' model lets you fork agents, branch personalities, and `git log` an agent's memory — a fundamentally different abstraction from OpenClaw's channel-centric personal assistant model.

Architecturally it ships as a Node/TypeScript CLI + SDK (with a slim core package split from the voice UI to satisfy supply-chain scanners), plus a newer Rust rewrite called 'ira' that powers a Tauri desktop app (Lyzr Edgespace) with an embedded web UI, Ollama-based local model management, and an onboarding wizard. It supports MCP servers (stdio + http/sse), declarative YAML tools, lifecycle hooks, and an OpenAI-compatible API surface.

Recent commits show serious engineering hygiene: two hardening batches closed a load-time RCE via shell-interpolated `git clone`, fixed tool concurrency races, wired real abort/steer semantics, and eliminated e2b VM and credential leaks — all with regression tests. Telemetry work groups model requests into per-turn traces. Compared to OpenClaw, GitClaw is more developer-infrastructure than end-user assistant: stronger on auditability and git workflows, weaker on messaging-channel breadth and community scale.
